title: Prohibit undisclosed AI-generated synthetic voice or likeness in mass political communications
description: Illustrative reference decision modelled on the FCC's response to the New Hampshire AI-generated Biden robocall. Not a documented decision of any specific organisation.

history.note: Initial Phase 2A seed content, part of the Foundational Twenty.

decision_statement: Any mass communication (robocall, broadcast, mass text) using an AI-generated or AI-cloned voice or likeness must carry a clear, audible or visible disclosure that the content is AI-generated, and platforms/carriers that detect synthetic voice content in political communications must flag it before further distribution rather than relying solely on after-the-fact enforcement.
decision_context: Motivated by the FCC's finding that an AI-cloned voice of a sitting president was used in a robocall campaign attempting to suppress primary-election turnout, leading to the FCC's ruling that AI-generated voices are 'artificial' voices subject to existing robocall regulation.
governing_body: Illustrative example — Election Integrity & Synthetic Media Governance Board
alternatives_considered: Rely entirely on after-the-fact enforcement against bad actors rather than upstream detection/disclosure.
Limit the disclosure requirement to broadcast media, excluding robocalls and mass text.

citations.title: FCC Makes AI-Generated Voices in Robocalls Illegal

relationships.reason: This decision is modelled as a direct governance response to this incident.
The decision is put into practice via this design pattern.
Disclosure requirements directly address the manipulative-technique concern this control describes.
Compliance must be demonstrated by a documented disclosure log.
Boards adopting this decision should be asking about deepfake detection and rapid-response readiness.
